title: The 5 Largest Lakes on Earth, Ranked (#1 Is Called a Sea)

scenes.text: Number one is called a sea. It is bigger than the next four lakes combined.

scenes.label: Lake Michigan · 58,000 km²
scenes.text: Number five: Lake Michigan. About fifty-eight thousand square kilometers of fresh water, and it just makes the list.

scenes.label: Lake Huron · 60,000 km²
scenes.text: Number four: Lake Huron. About sixty thousand square kilometers. That makes three Great Lakes in the top five.

scenes.label: Lake Victoria · 69,000 km²
scenes.text: Number three: Lake Victoria in Africa. About sixty-nine thousand square kilometers, shared by three countries.

scenes.label: Lake Superior · 82,000 km²
scenes.text: Number two: Lake Superior. About eighty-two thousand square kilometers, the largest of the Great Lakes.

scenes.label: Caspian Sea · 371,000 km²
scenes.text: Number one: the Caspian Sea. About three hundred and seventy thousand square kilometers, with no outlet to any ocean.

description:
The five largest lakes on Earth, ranked by surface area.
Three are Great Lakes, one is in Africa, and the biggest of all has the word sea in its name and no way out to the ocean.
Which of these would you want to sail across?
first_comment: Is the Caspian a lake or a sea in your book? And what should we rank next?
